title: License Plate Reader Company Seeks Partnership With Dashcam Company, Which Isn't Scary At All - Jalopnik

agency_candidates.display_name: New York City Department of Environmental Protection PD

summary: Jalopnik reports on Flock Safety's potential partnership with dashcam maker Nexar, which could expand ALPR surveillance by tapping into Nexar's network of connected dashcams uploading trillions of images monthly. The article raises privacy concerns about aggregating public location data into searchable databases accessible to government agencies and private buyers.

key_quotes.quote: It is in no way scary or ominous that such a partnership has the technological potential to turn private dashcams into surveillance tools.
404 Media reports that both Customs and Border Protection and ICE have used Flock's data to carry out their unpopular activities.
Adding data gathered from consumer dashcams to this database would expand its reach far beyond Flock's existing stationary cameras.
